description: Empirically measured sustained throughput and bandwidth on the Trn2 campaign device (one logical NeuronCore, LNC=2), copied verbatim from the TileArena calibration profile (not an AWS datasheet value). Intended as the Trn2 P_emp / BW_emp of the empirical SOL T_SOL = max(F / P_emp[mode], Q / BW_emp).

source.calibration_manifest_entry: not registered (candidate; tilebench/llm/v2/manifests/calibration.yaml devices.Trn2 stays status none until the owner decides)

scope.llc_note: SBUF capacity of the two physical cores used as the 'last-level' capacity for HBM eligibility; Trn2 has no hardware cache between HBM and SBUF
scope.name: AWS Trainium2 (NeuronCore-v3)
scope.note: one logical NeuronCore (LNC=2: two physical NeuronCore-v3), NEURON_RT_NUM_CORES=1: the scope on which NKI candidates and the formal TileBench NKI results are timed. Rates are per logical NeuronCore. Per-physical-core values are diagnostics measured with one core active; the whole device (4 logical / 8 physical cores) was not measured and is never obtained by scaling.

flags: saturation_not_demonstrated: best point is the last registered one and exceeds the runner-up by 21.3%
bf16x2_fma_vector.resource_scope: per logical NeuronCore (LNC=2: two physical NeuronCore-v3)
limitations: NKI nisa.tensor_scalar(multiply, add) chains on SBUF-resident tiles over VectorE / ScalarE / GpSimd (2 FLOP per element per instruction); Trn2 has no packed-pair FMA instruction, so the fp16x2/bf16x2 modes are FMA on fp16/bf16 tiles; exp/compare/convert/reduce instruction rates are not measured

limitations: control only: IEEE fp32 eager matmul (error <= 1e-5 vs float64), never a scoring ceiling

meaning.meaning: sustained streaming bandwidth of device memory (read+write copy probes), working sets far above the last-level cache

hbm_stream_bw.resource_scope: per logical NeuronCore (LNC=2: two physical NeuronCore-v3)
limitations: NKI DMA copies (HBM->SBUF->HBM and HBM->HBM) and eager copy_ on one logical NeuronCore; read+write bytes; the bandwidth one logical core can drive, not the device total

mma_bf16_f32acc.resource_scope: per logical NeuronCore (LNC=2: two physical NeuronCore-v3)
limitations: eager torch.matmul on torch.device('neuron') (neuronx-cc compiled) on square shapes 4096..16384, one logical NeuronCore (2 physical cores); the sustained rate of this compiler path, not a proof of the hardware maximum; TensorE activity throttling, if any, is part of the sustained rate

limitations: eager torch.matmul on torch.device('neuron') (neuronx-cc compiled) on square shapes 4096..16384, one logical NeuronCore (2 physical cores); the sustained rate of this compiler path, not a proof of the hardware maximum; TensorE activity throttling, if any, is part of the sustained rate

mma_tf32_f32acc.resource_scope: per logical NeuronCore (LNC=2: two physical NeuronCore-v3)
limitations: eager torch.matmul on torch.device('neuron') (neuronx-cc compiled) on square shapes 4096..16384, one logical NeuronCore (2 physical cores); the sustained rate of this compiler path, not a proof of the hardware maximum; TensorE activity throttling, if any, is part of the sustained rate
mma_tf32_f32acc.precision_path: neuronx-cc --auto-cast matmult --auto-cast-type tf32 on eager fp32 torch.matmul; TF32 identified by the error window [5e-5, 2e-3] vs float64 (the default fp32 matmul is IEEE, error <= 1e-5)

int32_vector.reason: no probe registered (as on every device)

mma_fp8_e4m3_f32acc.reason: NeuronCore-v3 TensorE takes the legacy float8_e4m3 format, not OCP float8_e4m3fn (installed nki 0.7 nc_matmul docs: e4m3fn from NeuronCore-v4); eager torch._scaled_mm(e4m3fn) produces no device execution (host path)

mma_fp8_e5m2_f32acc.reason: supported by TensorE (float8_e5m2, double_row) but declared by no Trn2 task; not measured

mma_int8_i32acc.reason: NeuronCore-v3 TensorE has no int8 input type (installed nki 0.7 nc_matmul: float8_e4m3/float8_e5m2/bfloat16/float16/tfloat32/float32); eager torch._int_mm returns a correct int32 result but produces no device execution (host path), so no device rate exists

notes: value is the exact number stored in the profile (unit as stored: byte/s, FLOP/s, OP/s); value_scaled = value / 1e9 (GB/s) or value / 1e12 (TFLOP/s) for readability only.

All values are per logical NeuronCore (LNC=2, two physical NeuronCore-v3, NEURON_RT_NUM_CORES=1), the scope on which NKI kernels are timed. per_physical_core_diagnostic entries were measured with one of the two cores active and are not scoring values; whole-device rates (4 logical / 8 physical cores) were not measured and must not be derived by multiplying.
Timing: device busy time per execution from the Neuron runtime trace (the formal TileBench NKI method), no host interval; compilation and warmup outside the timed sessions.
mma_tf32_f32acc uses neuronx-cc --auto-cast matmult --auto-cast-type tf32 on fp32 operands; the default eager fp32 matmul is IEEE (gemm_fp32_ieee, control only).
fp32_fma_vector / fp16x2_fma_vector / bf16x2_fma_vector are NKI multiply-add chains on VectorE, ScalarE and GpSimd (Trn2 has no packed-pair FMA; the 16-bit modes are FMA on fp16/bf16 tiles).
mma_int8_i32acc and mma_fp8_e4m3_f32acc are unsupported on this device path (see modes_not_calibrated).
The legacy tilebench/data/peak_performance/Trainium2.json is unchanged; its 577.7 GB/s is an older torch-xla measurement and its compute entries are not empirical.
This file is a data-only copy; the scoring path reads the profile through manifests/calibration.yaml, not this file.
